dropped.finding: The rewritten enforcement-flip runbook still has `verify.require_environment` / `opcert_enforce_since` set in the authoritative `rebar.toml`, with only the trust list in the gate job's environment. ADR 0125 decision 4 says to set all three together in the gate's own environment, which the change under test cannot edit. With `require_environment` in the shared `rebar.toml`, every environment that reads it but has no list refuses all certificates. That includes the developer clones and review bot that ADR 0125 says have no list. The runbook admits this but does not reconcile it with the ADR.
scenarios: An operator flips per the runbook. Every developer clone reads `require_environment` from `rebar.toml` and has no trust list, so local `claim` / plan-review consumption refuses every certificate with `foreign_key`.

docs/adr/0125-opcert-trust-per-environment.md:70-72 says the list lives in the user config etc. 'and the repository's own `rebar.toml` does not set it' -- a convention, not a check
dropped.finding: The docs say verify.trusted_opcert_keys lives in the verifying environment's own config (user config, env var, CI variables) and 'never the repository's rebar.toml'. The code does not enforce this: the project rebar.toml ranks above the user config, so a repository or branch can replace a developer's user-config trust list with keys it chooses.
scenarios: A developer sets trusted_opcert_keys in ~/.config/rebar/config.toml as documented, then checks out a branch whose rebar.toml adds `[verify] trusted_opcert_keys = ["9f1c8e42-... ssh-ed25519 <attacker key>"]`. The local plan-review and close checks then accept certificates the attacker made with their own key that name the trusted environment, since the environment is only a claim the certificate makes about itself.

A CI gate that sets require_environment but is missing the REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS job variable (runbook precondition 3) reads the list from the change's own rebar.toml, so the change under test supplies the keys it is checked against.
dropped.suggested_fix: In the config loader, refuse verify.trusted_opcert_keys (and arguably verify.require_environment's trust inputs) when it comes from the 'project' layer, raising ConfigError so verification fails closed. Until then, change docs/manifest-signing.md:43 to say that the user config is outranked by a project rebar.toml and that REBAR_VERIFY_TRUSTED_OPCERT_KEYS is the only setting a repository cannot override.
